snapshot: WHO African Region. The country is fighting the largest Ebola outbreak in its history, caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment. Conflict in the east and community mistrust make the response harder.

leadership.role: Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare
leadership.name: Samuel Roger Kamba

agenda.title: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak
agenda.text: As of 5 November 2026 the DRC had reported 10,741 confirmed cases and 5,230 deaths across eight provinces (Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uélé, Bas-Uélé, South Ubangi and North Ubangi). The outbreak was announced in mid-May. Ituri is the epicentre. Minister Kamba said in August that Ervebo would first go to front-line workers and contacts of patients; it is licensed against the Zaire strain, and WHO plans trials to test whether it protects against Bundibugyo.

agenda.title: Response under conflict and mistrust
agenda.text: Fighting between the M23 rebel group and government forces makes it hard to bring supplies to remote areas, and many communities distrust the response. Minister Kamba has warned that a response is practically impossible in occupied zones.

agenda.title: US health agreement and the end of US funding for health workers
agenda.text: A February 2026 bilateral health agreement with the United States provides US$900 million over five years. It requires sharing outbreak specimens and data within five days of a US request. The United States is due to stop paying Congolese health workers at the end of 2026, and the State Department has not said whether that deadline will be extended. The deal was signed before the Ebola outbreak was detected.

nl.text: One person linked to the outbreak was medically evacuated to the Netherlands (ECDC, 6 November 2026). Further Dutch links come from the NPHI Collaboration Map.
